body.statement:
For every \(N\in\mathbb N\) and every \(s_N\in(0,1]\) for which \(\mathcal P_N(s_N)\) is nonempty, let \(\mathcal I_N^{\mathrm{inv}}\) be the profile-recentered rectangle in \(\operatorname{def:moment-inversion}\).  This rectangle is measurable and satisfies
\[
\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)}
\Pr_P\{\mu(P)\in\mathcal I_N^{\mathrm{inv}}\}\ge 1-\alpha,
\qquad
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)}
\mathbb E_P W(\mathcal I_N^{\mathrm{inv}})
\le C_\alpha\min\{1,(\sqrt N s_N)^{-1}\}.
\]
Consequently \(\mathcal I_N^{\mathrm{inv}}\in\mathfrak I_{N,\alpha}\) and
\[
\inf_{\mathcal I_N\in\mathfrak I_{N,\alpha}}
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)}\mathbb E_PW(\mathcal I_N)
\le C_\alpha\min\{1,(\sqrt N s_N)^{-1}\}.
\]
The full-box fallback is used only when \(\mathsf F_N=\{N<2k_\alpha\}\); hence its expected contribution is exactly zero for all \(N\ge2k_\alpha\), and therefore is \(o\{(\sqrt N s_N)^{-1}\}\) uniformly over \(s_N\in(0,1]\).
body.justification: Profile recentering makes the nonlinear feasible set nonempty, a calibrated data-driven moment radius gives uniform coverage, and the lower width remains conditional on legal same-shell alternatives.
body.gap: Andrews and Cheng establish generic identification-robust inversion, and Zhu establishes weak-factor honesty costs; neither provides a total finite-moment inversion rule, a simultaneous moment-ball guarantee, or the \(s_N\)-specific missing-mean modulus for this cohort system.
body.consumer: The result provides simultaneous uncertainty bands for all missing untreated means in the Veneto wage application and in interactive-fixed-effect event studies without relying on pointwise Wald linearization.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)\), and let
\[
\vartheta_0=\bigl(p,\Gamma,(m_c,H_c,\sigma_c)_{c=1}^C\bigr)
\]
be its primitive parameter.  Put \(q_0=4+\delta\).  Assumption \(\operatorname{ass:moment-radius}\), conditional Jensen's inequality, and the definition \(B=M_{\mathrm{mom}}^{1/q_0}\) give, for every \(c\),
\[
\|m_c\|_2
=\|\mathbb E_P(\lambda_i\mid C_i=c)\|_2
\le \{\mathbb E_P(\|\lambda_i\|_2^{q_0}\mid C_i=c)\}^{1/q_0}
\le B.
\tag{1}
\]
By \(\operatorname{ass:conditional-homoskedasticity}\),
\(\mathbb E_P(\|\varepsilon_i\|_2^2\mid C_i=c)=T\sigma_c^2\), because \(\operatorname{ass:error-mean}\) makes the conditional second moment equal to the trace of the conditional covariance.  Lyapunov's inequality and \(\operatorname{ass:moment-radius}\) therefore imply
\[
(T\sigma_c^2)^{q_0/2}
\le \mathbb E_P(\|\varepsilon_i\|_2^{q_0}\mid C_i=c)
\le M_{\mathrm{mom}},
\qquad
0\le\sigma_c\le B/\sqrt T\le B.
\tag{2}
\]
The actual conditional loading law witnesses \(m\in\mathfrak M_\lambda(H)\).  Equations (1)--(2), together with \(\operatorname{ass:positive-shares}\), \(\operatorname{ass:factor-normalization}\), \(\operatorname{ass:loading-covariance}\), \(\operatorname{ass:local-signal-gap}\), and \(\operatorname{ass:singular-shell}\), verify every constraint in \(\operatorname{def:primitive-moment-class}\).  Hence
\[
\vartheta_0\in\overline\Theta_N(s_N).
\tag{3}
\]

We next identify the observed moment vector generated by \(\vartheta_0\).  By \(\operatorname{ass:rank-two-factor-law}\) and \(\operatorname{ass:error-mean}\),
\[
\mathbb E_P\{J_cY_i(0)\mid C_i=c\}=\Gamma_{S_c}m_c.
\tag{4}
\]
Moreover, \(\operatorname{ass:loading-error-orthogonality}\) and \(\operatorname{ass:error-mean}\) make both conditional cross moments between \(\lambda_i\) and \(\varepsilon_i\) zero, while \(\operatorname{ass:conditional-homoskedasticity}\) gives the error second moment.  Thus
\[
\mathbb E_P\{J_cY_i(0)Y_i(0)'J_c'\mid C_i=c\}
=\Gamma_{S_c}(H_c+m_cm_c')\Gamma_{S_c}'+\sigma_c^2I_{|S_c|}.
\tag{5}
\]
Multiplication of (4)--(5) by \(p_c\), and inclusion of the cohort-indicator moment \(p_c\), agree coordinate by coordinate with the maps in \(\operatorname{def:moment-inversion}\) and \(\operatorname{def:robust-observed-moments}\).  Therefore
\[
g(\vartheta_0)=\theta(P).
\tag{6}
\]

Suppose first that \(N\ge2k_\alpha\).  Define
\[
E_N=\|\widehat\theta-\theta(P)\|_{\mathsf m},
\qquad
\mathcal E_N=\{E_N\le\widehat\rho_N\}.
\]
By (3), (6), and the definition of the profiled distance,
\[
d_N
=\min_{\vartheta\in\overline\Theta_N(s_N)}
\|g(\vartheta)-\widehat\theta\|_{\mathsf m}
\le \|g(\vartheta_0)-\widehat\theta\|_{\mathsf m}
=E_N.
\tag{7}
\]
On \(\mathcal E_N\), equations (6)--(7) yield
\[
\|g(\vartheta_0)-\widehat\theta\|_{\mathsf m}
=E_N\le\widehat\rho_N\le d_N+\widehat\rho_N,
\]
so \(\vartheta_0\in\mathcal C_N\).  By the definition of the coordinatewise enclosing rectangle, \((\Gamma m_c)_{c=1}^C=\mu(P)\) then belongs to \(\mathcal I_N^{\mathrm{inv}}\).  The coverage part of \(\operatorname{lem:robust-moment-ball}\) gives
\[
\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)}
\Pr_P\{\mu(P)\in\mathcal I_N^{\mathrm{inv}}\}
\ge \inf_{P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)}\Pr_P(\mathcal E_N)
\ge1-\alpha.
\tag{8}
\]
If \(N<2k_\alpha\), the rule instead returns \([-B,B]^{CT}\).  From \(\Gamma'\Gamma=I_2\) and (1),
\[
|\mu_{ct}(P)|\le\|\Gamma m_c\|_2\le\|m_c\|_2\le B,
\]
so the fallback rectangle covers with probability one.  This proves honesty for every \(N\).

For completeness, the returned endpoints are measurable.  Write \(K_N=\overline\Theta_N(s_N)\), let \((\vartheta_\ell)_{\ell\ge1}\) be a deterministic countable dense subset of this compact finite-dimensional set, and let \(h_j(\vartheta)\) be target coordinate \(j\).  The function
\[
d(x)=\min_{\vartheta\in K_N}\|g(\vartheta)-x\|_{\mathsf m}
\]
is continuous because
\[
|d(x)-d(y)|\le\|x-y\|_{\mathsf m}.
\]
For \(r>0\), define
\[
u_{j,k}(x,r)
=\sup\bigl\{h_j(\vartheta_\ell):
\|g(\vartheta_\ell)-x\|_{\mathsf m}<d(x)+r+k^{-1}\bigr\}.
\]
Each \(u_{j,k}\) is measurable as a countable supremum of measurable functions after assigning the fixed lower bound \(-B\) to an infeasible index.  Compactness, continuity of \(g\) and \(h_j\), and density imply
\[
\lim_{k\to\infty}u_{j,k}(x,r)
=\max_{\substack{\vartheta\in K_N:\\
\|g(\vartheta)-x\|_{\mathsf m}\le d(x)+r}}h_j(\vartheta).
\tag{9}
\]
Indeed, dense approximants prove the lower inequality in (9), while any sequence approaching the left-hand supremum has a convergent subsequence whose limit satisfies the weak constraint and proves the upper inequality.  Applying the same argument to \(-h_j\) gives a measurable lower endpoint.  Since \(\widehat\rho_N>0\) is measurable, (9) proves measurability of every endpoint evaluated at \((\widehat\theta,\widehat\rho_N)\).  The small-sample box is deterministic, so the entire rule is measurable.

It remains to bound width.  For arbitrary \(\vartheta,\widetilde\vartheta\in\mathcal C_N\), the triangle inequality and (7) give, without conditioning on \(\mathcal E_N\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|g(\vartheta)-g(\widetilde\vartheta)\|_{\mathsf m}
&\le \|g(\vartheta)-\widehat\theta\|_{\mathsf m}
 +\|g(\widetilde\vartheta)-\widehat\theta\|_{\mathsf m}\\
&\le2(d_N+\widehat\rho_N)\\
&\le2(E_N+\widehat\rho_N).
\end{aligned}
\tag{10}
\]
Both parameters in (10) belong to \(\overline\Theta_N(s_N)\).  Applying \(\operatorname{lem:observed-moment-inverse-modulus}\) and absorbing the factor two into its constant yields
\[
\max_{c\in[C]}
\|\Gamma m_c-\widetilde\Gamma\widetilde m_c\|_\infty
\le K\min\left\{1,\frac{E_N+\widehat\rho_N}{s_N}\right\}.
\tag{11}
\]
For each target coordinate, compactness makes both extrema in the enclosing rectangle attainable; choosing their two attaining parameters in (11) shows that the maximal rectangle half-width is at most one half of the right side of (11).  Since \(x\mapsto\min\{1,x\}\) is increasing and concave on \([0,\infty)\), Jensen's inequality and the expectation part of \(\operatorname{lem:robust-moment-ball}\) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)}
\mathbb E_PW(\mathcal I_N^{\mathrm{inv}})
&\le K\min\left\{1,
\frac{\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)}
\mathbb E_P(E_N+\widehat\rho_N)}{s_N}\right\}\\
&\le K\min\left\{1,\frac{K_\alpha}{\sqrt N s_N}\right\}\\
&\le C_\alpha\min\{1,(\sqrt N s_N)^{-1}\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{12}
\]
For \(N<2k_\alpha\), the normalized width is at most one.  Because \(s_N\le1\) and \(N<2k_\alpha\),
\[
\min\{1,(\sqrt N s_N)^{-1}\}\ge(2k_\alpha)^{-1/2};
\]
increasing \(C_\alpha\) makes (12) valid also in this case.  Membership in \(\mathfrak I_{N,\alpha}\) follows from (8) and the small-sample argument, and the infimum bound follows by evaluating the infimum at \(\mathcal I_N^{\mathrm{inv}}\).  Finally, \(\mathsf F_N=\{N<2k_\alpha\}\) is deterministic and false whenever \(N\ge2k_\alpha\).  Its expected width contribution is then exactly zero, which divided by the positive scale \((\sqrt N s_N)^{-1}\) remains zero uniformly over \(s_N\in(0,1]\).  This proves every assertion.
